userStories.title: GitLab merge-request listing in the auto-review pass
userStories.description:
**Goal** — List connected GitLab repositories' open merge requests with their read credentials and feed eligible heads into the existing automatic REVIEW dispatcher.

**Motivation** — Even with the guard removed, auto-review would not run: `PrismaFleetRepoRepository.findAutoReviewPage` selects only `provider: 'github'` rows with an installation, and `FleetPrReviewPass.pollRepo` mints a GitHub installation token and calls `GitHubAppClient.listOpenPullRequests`.

**Approach** — The GitLab path mirrors the GitHub one call for call:

| Step | GitHub today | GitLab after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Which repos the pass reads | `provider: 'github'`, `githubInstallationId` not null | also `provider: 'gitlab'` with a `gitlabCredential` row |
| Token | `mintInstallationToken(installationId, name)` | `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo, 'read', fn)` |
| Open PR list | `listOpenPullRequests(token, owner, name)` | `GitLabAccessChecker.listOpenMergeRequests(access, fullName)` |
| Eligibility, claim, dispatch | `ReviewHeadDispatcher.dispatchRepo` | unchanged; it reads only `OpenPullRequest` fields |

One `GitLabRepoCredentials.call` wraps the single listing request, so a 401 marks the read token invalid through
`call` (feature 1 behaviour) and a rotated token is not marked by another request.

`listOpenMergeRequests` returns the existing `OpenPullRequest` shape so that `ReviewHeadDispatcher` does not change.
The dispatcher skips a pull request whose `headRepoFullName` is null or differs from `<owner>/<name>` (forks and
deleted heads, `review-head-dispatcher.ts` `skips`). A GitLab merge request does not carry its source project's
path, only `source_project_id`, so the client takes the repo's full name and reports it for a merge request whose
`source_project_id` equals the access target's project id, and null for any other (a fork). The pass passes
`` `${repo.owner}/${repo.name}` ``, so the dispatcher's comparison holds for same-project merge requests.

Changed. The baseline is listed only to find the code; implement the target.

- `GitLabAccessChecker` (`apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/gitlab-access-checker.ts`)
  - Target: adds `listOpenMergeRequests(access: GitLabAccess, fullName: string): Promise<OpenPullRequest[]>`. It runs
    the class's host check (`guard`) first, then sends `GET <apiBase>/projects/<projectId>/merge_requests?state=opened&per_page=100`
    with the `private-token` header. For each item: `number` = `iid`, `headSha` = `sha`, `draft` = `draft === true ||
    work_in_progress === true`, `updatedAt` = `new Date(updated_at)`, `headRepoFullName` = `fullName` when
    `source_project_id === access.target.projectId`, else null. Status mapping: 200 parses; 404 is
    `repo_not_found`; anything else goes through the class's `fail` (401 `gitlab_token_invalid`, 403
    `app_permissions_insufficient`, other `provider_error`). A body that is not an array, or an item whose `iid` is not
    a number, whose `updated_at` is not a string, or whose `sha` is neither a string nor null, is `provider_error`.
    An item whose `sha` is null (a merge request with no commits yet) is left out of the result, so it cannot block
    the review of the repo's other merge requests.
- `FleetPrReviewPass` (`apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/fleet-pr-review.pass.ts`)
  - Target: `constructor(repos, gate, github, dispatcher, @Inject(FLEET_CFG) config, gitlabCredentials: GitLabRepoCredentials, gitlab: GitLabAccessChecker)`
    (new dependencies appended). Inside the same `runAsSystem` body and after the same `gate.check`, `pollRepo` reads
    the list with `this.gitlabCredentials.call(repo, 'read', (access) => this.gitlab.listOpenMergeRequests(access, `${repo.owner}/${repo.name}`))`
    when `repo.provider === 'gitlab'`, and with the existing GitHub mint and `listOpenPullRequests` otherwise. Both
    lists go to the same `dispatcher.dispatchRepo` call. The existing catch (warning naming the repo id and
    `errorName(error)`) covers both providers.
- `PrismaFleetRepoRepository.findAutoReviewPage(limit)` (`apps/api/src/fleet/repos/prisma-fleet-repo.repository.ts`)
  - Target: `where: { autoReview: true, project: { deletedAt: null }, OR: [{ provider: 'github', githubInstallationId: { not: null } }, { provider: 'gitlab', gitlabCredential: { isNot: null } }] }`,
    same `orderBy: { id: 'asc' }` and `take: limit`.

Failure handling: listing 401 is gitlab_token_invalid, 404 repo_not_found, 403 app_permissions_insufficient, other statuses or malformed bodies provider_error, and a blocked host gitlab_host_blocked before any request. A deleted credential row resolves as gitlab_credentials_missing. The existing per-repo catch warns with repo id and error reason and continues to the next repo in all these cases; do not turn auto-review off.

Test implementation: create apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/fleet-pr-review.pass.gitlab.spec.ts exercising the public run(now) seam with a call mock that invokes the callback. Append credential/client mocks to the existing five-argument build() in fleet-pr-review.pass.spec.ts and retain every GitHub assertion. Add listing cases to gitlab-access-checker.spec.ts titled MR-1 onward; add the listing as a row to existing shared tables "AC-11: %s maps HTTP failures" (401, 403, 500) and "AC-12: %s blocks loopback hosts before requesting", keeping every existing case/row. Extend test/integration/fleet/fleet-repo-auto-review.integration.spec.ts for relation-present and relation-absent GitLab repos while preserving the GitHub AC-9 installation exclusion and existing ordering/limit coverage. Module imports/exports already provide both new dependencies; keep DI tests DB-free. The pass tests mock call and do not reassert token-invalid marking or absence of tokens in logs.

**Scope** — In: GitLab client listing, repository polling eligibility, provider branch in the pass, and their unit/integration tests. Out: US-002 setting enable guards; US-003 switch visibility; flow support, fork review, pagination past 100, inbound webhooks, short-lived token minting, token-driven automatic disabling and nax changes. The listing host check and 403/500 mapping reuse existing shared test tables rather than becoming separate listing acceptance criteria.

**Interface** — Spec declarations (unchanged except the new listing and appended constructor dependencies):
```typescript
listOpenMergeRequests(access: GitLabAccess, fullName: string): Promise<OpenPullRequest[]>
constructor(repos, gate, github, dispatcher, @Inject(FLEET_CFG) config, gitlabCredentials: GitLabRepoCredentials, gitlab: GitLabAccessChecker)
ReviewHeadDispatcher.dispatchRepo(repo: FleetRepoRecord, prs: readonly OpenPullRequest[], opts: DispatchRepoOptions): Promise<number>
OpenPullRequest { number: number; headSha: string; draft: boolean; headRepoFullName: string | null; updatedAt: Date }
GitLabRepoCredentials.call<T>(repo: { id: string; host?: string }, kind: 'read' | 'write', fn: (access: GitLabAccess) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>
GitLabAccess { token: string; target: { apiBase: string; projectId: number } }
EnablerGate.check(repo: FleetRepoRecord): Promise<PrincipalRef | null>
```
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] GitLabAccessChecker.listOpenMergeRequests(access, 'grp/app') sends GET <access.target.apiBase>/projects/<access.target.projectId>/merge_requests?state=opened&per_page=100 with the private-token header set to access.token.

AC-2 [unit] When a 200 answer holds one item { iid: 7, sha: 'abc', draft: false, updated_at: '2026-11-17T00:00:00Z', source_project_id: <access.target.projectId> }, listOpenMergeRequests returns [{ number: 7, headSha: 'abc', draft: false, headRepoFullName: 'grp/app', updatedAt: new Date('2026-11-17T00:00:00Z') }].
AC-3 [unit] listOpenMergeRequests returns an item with draft: true when the response item has draft: true.
AC-4 [unit] listOpenMergeRequests returns an item with draft: true when the response item has work_in_progress: true and no draft field.
AC-5 [unit] listOpenMergeRequests returns an item with headRepoFullName: null when its source_project_id differs from access.target.projectId.
AC-6 [unit] listOpenMergeRequests throws RepoCheckException with reason provider_error when a response item's sha is the number 5.
AC-7 [unit] When a 200 answer holds one item with sha: null and one valid item, listOpenMergeRequests returns only the valid item.
AC-8 [unit] listOpenMergeRequests throws RepoCheckException with reason gitlab_token_invalid when the listing answers 401.
AC-9 [unit] listOpenMergeRequests throws RepoCheckException with reason repo_not_found when the listing answers 404.
AC-10 [integration] PrismaFleetRepoRepository.findAutoReviewPage(50) returns a GitLab repo with autoReview: true and a FleetRepoGitlabCredential row.
AC-11 [integration] PrismaFleetRepoRepository.findAutoReviewPage(50) does not return a GitLab repo with autoReview: true and no FleetRepoGitlabCredential row.

AC-12 [unit] Given one enabled GitLab repo { provider: 'gitlab', owner: 'grp', name: 'app' } on the page, FleetPrReviewPass.run(now) calls GitLabRepoCredentials.call with the repo record itself (the page's row, carrying its host) and 'read', calls GitLabAccessChecker.listOpenMergeRequests with the access call resolved and 'grp/app', and calls ReviewHeadDispatcher.dispatchRepo with the repo and the list it returned.

AC-13 [unit] Given an enabled GitLab repo whose row also carries a non-null githubInstallationId (9n), FleetPrReviewPass.run(now) never calls GitHubAppClient.mintInstallationToken or GitHubAppClient.listOpenPullRequests.

AC-14 [unit] When GitLabRepoCredentials.call rejects with RepoCheckException('gitlab_token_invalid') for the first of two enabled repos, FleetPrReviewPass.run(now) logs a warning containing the first repo's id and gitlab_token_invalid, and still calls ReviewHeadDispatcher.dispatchRepo for the second repo.

AC-15 [unit] When GitLabRepoCredentials.call rejects with RepoCheckException('gitlab_credentials_missing') for the first of two enabled repos, FleetPrReviewPass.run(now) logs a warning containing the first repo's id and gitlab_credentials_missing, and still calls ReviewHeadDispatcher.dispatchRepo for the second repo.

routing.reasoning: Three runtime-file changes add a standard client method, widen an existing Prisma filter and reuse the established credential-call branch without new abstractions; read-token handling and host confinement still require the strict security strategy.

suggestedCriteria: GitLabAccessChecker.listOpenMergeRequests throws RepoCheckException with reason provider_error when a 200 response body is not an array.
GitLabAccessChecker.listOpenMergeRequests throws RepoCheckException with reason provider_error when a response item's iid is not a number.
GitLabAccessChecker.listOpenMergeRequests throws RepoCheckException with reason provider_error when a response item's updated_at is not a string.

modifiedFiles.reason: `build()` constructs `FleetPrReviewPass` with five arguments; it now passes `GitLabRepoCredentials` and `GitLabAccessChecker` mocks as the sixth and seventh. Every existing GitHub assertion stays.

gains the `listOpenMergeRequests` cases; `listOpenMergeRequests` is also added as a row to the shared tables "AC-11: %s maps HTTP failures" (401, 403, 500) and "AC-12: %s blocks loopback hosts before requesting". The new cases are titled from `MR-1` on, so they do not reuse that file's `AC-n` titles. Every existing case and row stays.
gains the GitLab listing cases (AC-10, AC-11); "AC-9: excludes enabled repos without a GitHub installation" stays and still holds for a GitHub row.

userStories.title: Enable guards for auto-review and trusted detected checks on GitLab
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Allow connected GitLab repos to enable automatic reviews and trusted detected checks while refusing missing credentials with the provider-specific 422 reason.

**Motivation** — After features 1-3, a connected GitLab repo can run every job kind, but two repo settings still refuse it:

- `FleetReposService.configureAutoReview` throws `AutoReviewException('github app required')` for any repo that
  is not a GitHub repo with an installation;
- `FleetReposService.configureFixChecks` throws `FixChecksException('github app required')` the same way.

**Approach** — The enable guard follows `configureFixUnprotected`, which feature 2 already opened to GitLab: a GitLab row needs a
`gitlabCredential` row (absent or null is refused `gitlab credentials required`); a GitHub row still needs an
installation (`github app required`). Disabling is never refused. The 422 message is the existing
`fleet.autoReview` / `fleet.fixChecks` template with `{reason}`, so no new i18n key is needed in the API.

- `FleetReposService.configureAutoReview` and `FleetReposService.configureFixChecks` (`apps/api/src/fleet/repos/fleet-repos.service.ts`)
  - Target: enabling throws `github app required` when `row.provider === 'github' && row.githubInstallationId === null`,
    and `gitlab credentials required` when `row.provider === 'gitlab' && row.gitlabCredential == null`. Everything
    after the guard is unchanged.

Failure handling: enabling either setting for a GitLab row without credentials answers 422 with reason gitlab credentials required; nothing is stored and no audit is recorded. Use the existing exception classes and translated templates. Do not add token-health validation or forge requests to enabling: credential row existence is the target. Existing transaction boundaries, auto-review caller dispatch permission, profile validation, enabled-by attribution/timestamps, and fix-checks audit summary remain unchanged. In particular, fix-checks still adds no dispatch-permission requirement, and disabling remains allowed for either provider.

Test implementation: in apps/api/src/fleet/repos/fleet-repos.auto-review.spec.ts remove only { provider: 'gitlab' } from the shared "AC-9/AC-10 requires installed GitHub app: %o" table, preserving { githubInstallationId: null } and its github app required assertion. Add GitLab credential-present, null and absent cases. In fleet-repos.fix-checks.spec.ts remove only { provider: 'gitlab' } from the shared "refuses to enable on a repo without a GitHub App installation: %o" table; preserve the null-installation GitHub refusal and every disabling case and add separate GitLab cases. Update the old GitLab 422 expectations in test/integration/fleet/fleet-repo-auto-review-route.integration.spec.ts (AC-5) and fleet-repo-fix-checks-route.integration.spec.ts (AC-3) to the new GitLab reason; add connected GitLab 200 cases. Preserve fix-checks route AC-4 for GitHub without installation. For the fix-checks refusal assert exactly 'Detected checks cannot be trusted: gitlab credentials required.' including its final period. Seed a real credential relation using test/integration/fleet/fleet-repo-fix-unprotected-route.integration.spec.ts as the pattern, without forge HTTP or token decryption. Keep all approval, auth, transaction and audit regression assertions. DB tests retain the shared gate and run through the host DB-enabled scoped test command, not merely as skipped sandbox suites.

**Scope** — In: provider-specific enable guards for both existing repo settings and corresponding service/route behavior tests. Out: US-001 polling query and GitLab MR listing; US-003 switch mounts; changes to disabling, GitHub refusals, assignment payload, nax checks or flows. No DTO, schema, permission-key, approval-policy or API translation-key changes.

**Interface** — Existing method signatures remain unchanged (source signatures):
```typescript
configureAutoReview(principal: UserPrincipal | AgentPrincipal, id: string, dto: UpdateAutoReviewDto): Promise<FleetRepoDto>
configureFixChecks(principal: UserPrincipal | AgentPrincipal, id: string, dto: UpdateFixChecksDto): Promise<FleetRepoDto>
```
Existing HTTP interfaces are PATCH /api/fleet/repos/:id/auto-review with { enabled: true } and PATCH /api/fleet/repos/:id/fix-checks with { trustDetectedChecks: true }, under the existing fleet.repo.review.configure approvable write. Successful responses retain their current FleetRepoDto envelope.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] FleetReposService.configureAutoReview(principal, id, { enabled: true }) for a GitLab row with a non-null gitlabCredential calls updateAutoReview with autoReview: true and the principal's id as autoReviewEnabledById.

AC-2 [unit] configureAutoReview(principal, id, { enabled: true }) for a GitLab row whose gitlabCredential is null throws AutoReviewException with reason 'gitlab credentials required' and status 422, and calls neither updateAutoReview nor audit.record.
AC-3 [unit] configureAutoReview(principal, id, { enabled: true }) for a GitLab row with no gitlabCredential field throws AutoReviewException with reason 'gitlab credentials required'.

AC-4 [unit] FleetReposService.configureFixChecks(principal, id, { trustDetectedChecks: true }) for a GitLab row with a non-null gitlabCredential calls updateFixChecks(id, true) and records the audit summary 'fix detected checks enabled'.

AC-5 [unit] configureFixChecks(principal, id, { trustDetectedChecks: true }) for a GitLab row whose gitlabCredential is null throws FixChecksException with reason 'gitlab credentials required' and status 422, and calls neither updateFixChecks nor audit.record.

AC-6 [integration] When the global admin sends PATCH /api/fleet/repos/:id/auto-review with { enabled: true } for a GitLab repo with a FleetRepoGitlabCredential row, the response is 200 with autoReview: true, and the stored row has autoReview: true.

AC-7 [integration] When PATCH /api/fleet/repos/:id/auto-review receives { enabled: true } for a GitLab repo without a credential row, the response is 422 whose body contains 'gitlab credentials required', and the stored row keeps autoReview: false.

AC-8 [integration] When the global admin sends PATCH /api/fleet/repos/:id/fix-checks with { trustDetectedChecks: true } for a GitLab repo with a FleetRepoGitlabCredential row, the response is 200 with fixTrustDetectedChecks: true.

AC-9 [integration] When PATCH /api/fleet/repos/:id/fix-checks receives { trustDetectedChecks: true } for a GitLab repo without a credential row, the response is 422 whose message is 'Detected checks cannot be trusted: gitlab credentials required.', and the stored row keeps fixTrustDetectedChecks: false.

routing.reasoning: Two narrow service guards reuse an established provider pattern with existing unit and route suites; credential-dependent enable decisions and approvable admin writes require the security override.

suggestedCriteria: configureFixChecks(principal, id, { trustDetectedChecks: true }) throws FixChecksException with reason 'gitlab credentials required' when a GitLab row has no gitlabCredential field.

modifiedFiles.reason: the shared table "AC-9/AC-10 requires installed GitHub app: %o" runs `{ provider: 'gitlab' }` and `{ githubInstallationId: null }` and asserts `github app required` for both; the `{ provider: 'gitlab' }` row is removed from that table (the `{ githubInstallationId: null }` row stays `github app required`), and separate GitLab cases are added: without a `gitlabCredential` (null, and absent) it is refused `gitlab credentials required`, with one it is enabled.

the shared table "refuses to enable on a repo without a GitHub App installation: %o" runs `{ provider: 'gitlab' }` and `{ githubInstallationId: null }` and asserts `github app required` for both; the `{ provider: 'gitlab' }` row is removed from that table (the `{ githubInstallationId: null }` row stays `github app required`), and separate GitLab cases are added: without a `gitlabCredential` it is refused `gitlab credentials required`, with one it is enabled.

"AC-5: enabling auto-review on a GitLab repo is 422 with the github app reason" pinned `github app required` for a GitLab repo without credentials; it now pins `gitlab credentials required`, and a GitLab repo with a credential row is enabled (200).

"AC-3: enabling on a GitLab repo answers 422 with the github app reason and stores nothing" pinned `Detected checks cannot be trusted: github app required`; it now pins `Detected checks cannot be trusted: gitlab credentials required` for a GitLab repo without credentials, and a GitLab repo with a credential row is enabled (200). "AC-4" for a GitHub repo without an installation stays.

userStories.title: Web switches for GitLab repos
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Show the existing automatic-review and trusted-detected-check switches on connected GitLab rows in the admin repos page.

**Motivation** — The admin repos page mounts the two switches only for a GitHub repo with an installation.

**Approach** — `apps/web/pages/admin/fleet/repos.vue`
  - Baseline: `FleetRepoAutoReview` and `FleetRepoFixChecks` mount under `v-if="repo.provider === 'github' && repo.githubInstallationId"`.
  - Target: both mount under the same condition `FleetRepoFixUnprotected` already uses:
    `(repo.provider === 'github' && repo.githubInstallationId) || (repo.provider === 'gitlab' && repo.gitlab !== null)`.

US-003 reads `FleetRepo.gitlab`, which feature 1 already returns on `GET /api/fleet/repos`; no new field.

Use the exact connection-existence predicate; do not add health/status restrictions. Keep FleetRepoFixUnprotected's mount, existing :repo bindings and @saved whole-row replacement handlers unchanged. Reuse RepoAutoReview.vue and RepoFixChecks.vue without duplicating settings logic: they already use the existing API composable, fleet.repo.review.configure permissions, pending approval notices, i18n labels and save/error behavior. This is Nuxt/Vue, not Next.js.

Test implementation (spec): `apps/web/tests/pages/admin-fleet-repos.spec.ts` — "GitLab FIX override mounts only for connected repos and keeps other controls GitHub-only (US-005 AC-1/2/3)" expects the connected GitLab row to hold one switch (`Allow fixes on an unprotected default branch`); it now holds three (`Enable automatic reviews`, `Trust detected checks for fixes`, `Allow fixes on an unprotected default branch`), so the whole-page `labels` list grows from four entries to six (three for the GitHub row, three for the connected GitLab row). The unconnected GitLab row still holds none, and the GitHub row without an installation still holds none.

Use row-scoped assertions for the two new GitLab mounts and keep the existing regression assertions for other rows. Do not add a page-level permission gate or change API authorization. No new strings, locales, composable contracts or files are required.

**Scope** — In: the two existing v-if conditions and the admin page's switch visibility assertions. Out: US-002 API enable guards and persistence; US-001 polling/listing; changes to GitHub or unconnected-repo switch behavior, credential registration/rotation, flow UI, global layout/navigation, nax checks and setup documentation.

**Interface** — Existing template predicate, verbatim:
```vue
v-if="(repo.provider === 'github' && repo.githubInstallationId) || (repo.provider === 'gitlab' && repo.gitlab !== null)"
```
Existing typed connection field from apps/web/lib/fleet-types.ts:
```typescript
gitlab: FleetRepoGitlab | null
```
Apply the predicate to both FleetRepoAutoReview and FleetRepoFixChecks, not to a newly created component or generated client.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] The admin repos page renders the 'Enable automatic reviews' switch in the row of a GitLab repo whose gitlab is not null.
AC-2 [unit] The admin repos page renders the 'Trust detected checks for fixes' switch in the row of a GitLab repo whose gitlab is not null.

routing.reasoning: Two existing v-if predicates and their page tests are a simple change with no new helpers; strict security routing is retained because the connected admin controls must preserve fleet.repo.review.configure denial, verified through the existing allowed: false harness.

modifiedFiles.reason: "GitLab FIX override mounts only for connected repos and keeps other controls GitHub-only (US-005 AC-1/2/3)" expects the connected GitLab row to hold one switch (`Allow fixes on an unprotected default branch`); it now holds three (`Enable automatic reviews`, `Trust detected checks for fixes`, `Allow fixes on an unprotected default branch`), so the whole-page `labels` list grows from four entries to six (three for the GitHub row, three for the connected GitLab row). The unconnected GitLab row still holds none, and the GitHub row without an installation still holds none.

analysis:
Refine audit: re-read .nax/features/gitlab-auto-review/spec.md:115-241 and the affected source. All 26 numbered spec criteria are retained in their original stories, with observable assertions and no deprecated file-content tags. Inventory: US-001 AC-1 exact GET/header; AC-2 complete same-project mapping and Date; AC-3 draft; AC-4 legacy work_in_progress without draft; AC-5 fork null head; AC-6 numeric SHA refusal; AC-7 null-SHA omission alongside a valid item; AC-8 401 reason; AC-9 404 reason; AC-10 connected GitLab included; AC-11 credentialless GitLab excluded; AC-12 exact page-row identity including host, read callback access/fullName and dispatcher handoff; AC-13 GitLab with installation 9n never calls either GitHub method; AC-14 invalid-token warning AND second-repo continuation; AC-15 missing-credential warning AND second-repo continuation. US-002 AC-1 enabling and principal attribution (principal.id is the stored scalar, as fleet-repos.service.ts:259 establishes); AC-2 null credential 422 with no write/audit; AC-3 absent credential refusal; AC-4 update and existing audit summary; AC-5 fix-checks null credential 422 with no write/audit; AC-6 admin auto-review 200 and persisted true; AC-7 auto-review 422 and stored false; AC-8 admin fix-checks 200 true; AC-9 exact English message including final period and stored false. US-003 AC-1 auto-review mount and AC-2 fix-checks mount on non-null gitlab. No qualifying clause was removed: in particular US-001 AC-12 retains the host-carrying page-row parenthetical and AC-14/15 retain continuation. All 16 feature-level exclusions match spec.md:128-145 verbatim; do not promote the excluded GitHub-without-installation, disabling, unconnected-row or payload behaviors into new ACs. Failure paths already exist in both API stories; add the previously missing web negative path as a permission-disabled rendering regression, not a new connection gate. Add a GitHub listing-call regression to US-001 for its extended constructor/provider branch; US-002 AC-4 protects the existing audit summary, and the web negative path protects existing component permission behavior. Context files contain all five/four/four spec recommendations respectively; the additional web test file fills, but does not exceed, its five-file limit. No dependencies or workdirs change. Reclassify US-001 as medium: its three runtime-file edits reuse established abstractions, despite their cross-module locations; credential handling still mandates three-session-tdd. Keep strict security routing for US-002 and for the admin-control permission regression in US-003. The PATCH connection-summary risk remains follow-up analysis only, not an implementation requirement or suggested criterion contradicting the guard-only scope.

Existing-system enhancement, not greenfield. The binding decomposition is US-001 (apps/api, no dependencies), US-002 (apps/api, no dependencies), US-003 (apps/web, depends only on US-002). The owner split GitLab parity F4 into this feature and deferred gitlab-flows; implement the supplied F4a targets rather than reopening the broader original parity design. Source of feature requirements: .nax/features/gitlab-auto-review/spec.md:1; the earlier parity design's feature map is docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-16-gitlab-parity-design.md:98. No codebase-memory MCP tools are exposed in this session, so discovery used direct Read/Grep tools in the supplied execution repository. No code or tests were executed while drafting this PRD.

Architecture and conventions: apps/api is NestJS on Fastify with Prisma 7 and Vitest, not a plain Fastify service; apps/web is Nuxt 4/Vue SSR with Jest, NOT Next.js despite the supplied package-detection metadata (.nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:24; .nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:24; apps/web/pages/admin/fleet/repos.vue:1). Keep business rules and persistence in the API and reuse Nuxt composables in web. Read the app contexts before implementation and the Nathapp capability catalog before writing NestJS code; the Nathapp docs MCP is not exposed in this drafting session. Forge calls use FleetHttpClient and its existing timeout/no-redirect behavior. Do not alter credential encryption, token selection, auth/approval boundaries, generated AGENTS.md files or generated CLI clients. US-001 and US-002 require three-session-tdd because they touch token use and credential-dependent enable guards. US-003 is a small template change but conservatively uses the same security override for credential-dependent admin controls.

US-001 implementation and call chain: FleetPrReviewPoller consumes FleetPrReviewPass.run (apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/fleet-pr-review.poller.ts:3,13). FleetPrReviewPass currently accepts five constructor arguments (apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/fleet-pr-review.pass.ts:42), reads a maximum page of 50, warns on a full page and maintains a pass-wide attempt cap (same file:59-72). pollRepo runs after the enabler gate in runAsSystem with the stored enabler onBehalfOf context, always mints a GitHub token and lists PRs today, and catches failures into a warning containing repo id plus errorName, returning already-counted attempts (same file:80-105). Append GitLabRepoCredentials and GitLabAccessChecker as constructor arguments six and seven. Branch on provider === 'gitlab', not installation-id presence, keeping the GitHub else path unchanged. One credentials.call(repo, 'read', callback) must wrap precisely one listOpenMergeRequests request and carry the exact page row including host. Forward both providers' lists to the unchanged dispatcher with the same now, pollMs, remaining and onAttempt options. Preserve runAsSystemWriter, gate ordering, enabler context, cap accounting, failure isolation and poller behavior.
